gen-gf-gochi-hand-switzer: Switzer is a Swiss-minded sans of wire-like, tubular letters with a high waist line and c tips that stay well apart. Shrink Gochi Hand and its crowded lowercase fades; best for a few words.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-work-sans: Gochi Hand crowds its lowercase up toward the cap line, hand-drawn and friendly. Gochi Hand does best with a quick hello, not long paragraphs; Work Sans, modern and thick-jointed, does the steadier talking.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: Wide-set and commanding, Goldman rounds its forms like open parentheses and gives every letter generous clearance. And Stint Ultra Expanded, a serif with pipe-cleaner strokes, lets each character float apart in the same wide spirit.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-stint-ultra-expan: Expressive from the first letter, Grandstander draws plain, constant-width lines. Stint Ultra Expanded, a serif of open counters, floats its characters apart and keeps a moderate lowercase height beneath it.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-hepta-slab: Gugi is distinctive and bold, its lowercase nearly reaching the capitals while open terminals let the counters flow outward. Hepta Slab, a dignified serif with a stretched-out look, then settles in with a moderate lowercase.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-kiwi-maru: Gugi does its best work as a display voice, its lowercase nearly reaching the capitals. Kiwi Maru, a serif with generous letterspace and terminals stopping far from the stem, does the quieter work of body copy.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-padyakke-expanded-one: Gugi is bold and distinctive, its lowercase nearly reaching the capitals and its curves matching its stems exactly. Padyakke Expanded One, a literary serif, spaces its glyphs like knots on a slack rope, each c opening wide.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: Stint Ultra Expanded feels authoritative and traditional, a serif whose characters float apart like pipe-cleaner shapes. Gugi handles the loud display work, while the serif handles the running text.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-archivo: Archivo reads editorial and approachable, a sans-serif whose curves open outward and whose x-height commands the line. Gveret Levin brings rope-thick, hand-drawn curves, the friendliest thing here, though not for lengthy paragraphs.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-fs-epilogue: Gveret Levin is friendly and hand-drawn, with a pronounced x-height. Epilogue, a sans-serif built on a wire-like monoline skeleton with stubby ascenders, works better at a modest size and with brief text.
